html:
Gondwana, the land of the Gonds, is the forested hill country of central India, in today's Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Chhattisgarh. On the 1492 map it marks the Gond kingdoms between the Deccan sultanates and the north.

The Gonds are one of India's largest tribal peoples. From about the 14th century Gond rulers founded kingdoms here, at Garha-Mandla on the Narmada, at Chanda, at Deogarh and at Kherla. They built forts and tanks and took on some customs of Hindu courts.

Garha-Mandla grew strongest. Its queen, Rani Durgavati, died fighting a Mughal army sent by Akbar in 1564. The other Gond kingdoms lasted longer, but in the 1700s the Bhonsle Marathas of Nagpur, part of the Maratha Confederacy, absorbed them.

The region gave its name to geology. In the 1800s geologists named a series of rock beds after it, and later the ancient southern supercontinent was called Gondwana after those rocks.
